cohort: The study participants were 395 singleton pregnancies undergoing second-trimester cervical-length screening at 18-21(+6) weeks of gestation.
finding: The presence of abnormal intra-amniotic structures (AIAS) around the internal cervical os was associated with significantly higher incidences of emergency cesarean section, abnormal placenta and umbilical cord, and abnormal deliveries, as well as greater blood loss during delivery, compared to control groups.
mod_finding: The incidence of emergency cesarean section was significantly higher in the AIAS group compared to both low-lying placenta and control groups.
